name: Scout Gallagher
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember entering a competition nobody in my family took seriously.” People around the downtown fountain know Scout by a small Wednesday habit. Scout keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I came second. I don't want to win by someone else's withdrawal and I don't want a dishonest result.
appearance: Scout has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a brown corduroy jacket with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. In conversation Scout grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Scout talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Scout's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To secure an honest result for the runner-up.
family: Loretta Osei is Scout’s aunt by marriage. Scout calls about good news first. Loretta is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The million-dollar flat*, Loretta says, “I am her sister. My own flat is barely worth half and it's the one with space for us both.”
connections: Aidan Henry. The juror's family recognition puts the runner-up in an awkward but legitimate position.

reactions.situation: A relative wants the manuscript returned unopened
reactions.response: Scout returns the pages privately without treating keeping them closed as a verdict on the work.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Scout agrees on a sum and a date with the friend in private, keeping the arrangement out of family gossip.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Scout says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
